transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?
I’ve started going out of my way to avoid any job that involves getting up high. When I absolutely can’t avoid it, I’m barely able to stay up there long enough to do my work.
Do you only experience this intense fear with heights, or do you also feel anxious and avoid other situations, like crowded places, public transit, or being far from home?

It’s strictly heights that get to me, like ladders, roofs, or high tree stands. I don’t have any trouble with crowds, public transit, or being far from home at all. Even my volunteering and fishing are only affected if they involve getting up high.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits a marked, persistent, and unreasonable fear of heights (ladders, roofs, high tree stands) that leads to active avoidance of jobs involving heights and severe distress when heights cannot be avoided. Other anxiety disorders, such as agoraphobia (F40.0), were ruled out as the patient does not experience anxiety in crowds, public transit, or when far from home.
